questions.q: What historical change does the summary blame for our culture of overwork?
a: The shift from task pay to hourly pay
The decline of agricultural labour
The rise of remote working
The introduction of the five-day week
questions.why: Lesson 1 traces today's long hours to the Industrial Revolution, when workers began being paid by the hour.

questions.q: What does the summary mean by polluted time?
a: Time off still filled with thoughts about work
Hours lost to endless social media scrolling
Time spent commuting to and from work
Days when your schedule is double-booked
questions.why: Lesson 2 describes polluted time as rest that is spoiled by mulling over emails and work problems.

questions.q: Why does the summary say hearing an actual human voice matters?
a: It creates a connection that text messages cannot
It conveys information more accurately
It saves time compared with writing
It is the only way to resolve conflicts
questions.why: Lesson 2 explains that a real voice humanises the speaker and builds a stronger bond than messaging.

questions.q: What health effects of isolation does the summary mention?
a: A higher risk of heart attacks and cancer
Mostly minor issues like poor sleep
A stronger immune system over time
Improved focus but lower empathy
questions.why: Lesson 2 says loneliness is emotionally painful and is linked to heart disease, cancer, and a shorter life.

questions.q: What first step does the summary recommend for improving your perception of time?
a: Keep a log of how you spend your time
Cut your to-do list in half
Set a strict limit on screen time
Schedule every hour of the day
questions.why: Lesson 3 suggests tracking everything, even mindless phone use, to see clearly where your time actually goes.
